note: Simulated scan sequences used for the live demo. Each demo names the graph profile it must run on, so DEMO 5 can reconfigure the graph before running.

demos.title: DEMO 1 - Valid journey
demos.explanation: Every consecutive pair of checkpoints is a legal edge of the standard graph, and the bag reaches the terminal state ARRIVAL.

demos.title: DEMO 2 - Duplicate scan
demos.explanation: The bag is already at SECURITY when SECURITY is scanned again. No self-loop exists in the graph, so the repeated scan is a duplicate, not a transition.

demos.title: DEMO 3 - Invalid transition
demos.explanation: SECURITY -> ARRIVAL is not an edge of the standard graph. The scan is rejected and the bag stays at SECURITY.

demos.title: DEMO 4 - Incomplete journey
demos.explanation: All observed transitions are legal and ARRIVAL is still reachable, but the bag has not been observed at ARRIVAL. It is incomplete, not invalid.

demos.title: DEMO 5 - Unreachable arrival
demos.explanation: This demo first switches the graph to the quarantine profile. The same scans as DEMO 4 stay legal, and ARRIVAL is reachable while the bag is at CHECK_IN and SECURITY. After LOADING -> QUARANTINE (a dead end) BFS proves ARRIVAL can no longer be reached; the first two events are merely INCOMPLETE.
